articleTitle: High Frequency Permeability Measurement of Magnetic Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A device for automated measurement of the permeability of thin films is described. Specimens are placed in a high frequency band magnetic field, and the induced emf measured using a differential detection coil, with a damping resistance inserted to prevent resonance. The frequency is varied to find the μ-f characteristic. The device was used to measure the characteristic of a sputtered Sendust film 4 mm by 4 μm up to 100 MHz; measurements required only a few minutes' time.

articleTitle: State of the Art in DC-to-DC Converters
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The switching regulator is a power supply in which the output voltage is regulated by ON and OFF processes of a power semiconductor element. This regulator has been used widely in almost all electronic equipment because of its small size and low power dissipation. However, switching regulators in use now do not always seem to be compatible with highly integrated electronic devices, as it is very difficult to apply IC techniques to such regulators. Even if the latest electronic techniques are used, switching regulators are still too large, too complicated and not always sufficiently reliable. In order to reduce the size of such regulators, the switching frequency should be made as high as possible. This means that the switching loss of the semiconductor and the core loss of the transformer and reactor should be low. The effective use of magnetic components will provide the solution for raising frequencies as well as making switching regulators more simple and reliable. In this paper, we describe the state of the art of switching regulators, and future trends in applications of magnetic components.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Writing System with the Pulse Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A pulse magnetic field was used successfully in magneto-optical writing of bits of size smaller than the diameter of the spot of light. Applying a pulse magnetic field to the medium, when the sum of the signal field and the diamagnetic field becomes larger than the coercive force, the magnetization in that area is inverted. Raising the pulse frequency caused the polarity to overlap with reverse magnetic domains, canceling to form a "crescent" smaller than the light spot. In experiments, a lens focused semiconductor laser light to 5.6 μm, and signal and bias fields of 30 and 300 Oe were used to write bits 0.45 &3x003BC;m in width and 2 μm in length.

abstract: Magnetic thin films of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> (x = 0.33 to 0.40) with perpendicular magnetization were obtained using the rf sputtering method for the first time. Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">66</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">34</inf> deposited onto an unheated substrate had K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> = 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> = 280 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>1 = 700 Oe. Film composition and substrate temperature during film preparation were the most important factors inducing perpendicular anisotropy. X-ray diffraction studies showed that the induction of perpendicular anisotropy was always accompanied by growth of the crystalline phase (Cr-dominant bcc phase). FeCr films also exhibited high corrosion resistivity in an oxidizing environment. FeCr is a candidate material for use in perpendicular magnetic recording.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Si-Ru Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors studied Fe-Si magnetic thin films with Ru added formed on glass substrates by RF sputtering. Addition of Ru tended to lower the saturation magnetic flux density, but the rate of decrease was smaller than for transition metals such as Cr. The permeability and coercive force remained unaffected. Polarization curve measurements and tests using salt sprays indicated that films with Ru added were more resistant to corrosion. Fe-Si-Ru alloys were obtained with a saturation flux density of about 1.7 T, a permeability of about 500 and a corrosive resistance comparable to that of Ni-Fe alloys.

articleTitle: Preparation and Magnetic Properties of Electrodeposited Permalloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Saccharin was added during preparation of Permalloy sample by electrodeposition in an attempt to reduce mechanical strain and improve the magnetic properties. For a constant film thickness T, the internal stress tended to decrease as saccharin was added to the plating bath. Dependences of coercive force H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and squareness ratio B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>/B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> on T and the amount of saccharin added were also found. The minimum H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> was obtained for a film thickness of 2 μm, regardless of whether saccharin was added; the addition of saccharin also had little effect on the squareness ratio.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic properties of amorphous Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-CaO-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are described in terms of the microscopic structure. The amorphous region and magnetization strengths for the system were determined, while measurements of the temperature dependence of magnetization revealed no clear Curie temperature; this was attributed to thermal decomposition of the ferrimagnetic crystalline phase. articleTitle: Microstructure and Coercivity of Nd-Fe-B Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to clarify the mechanism underlying the coercivity in Nd-Fe-B magnets, the authors studied both the magnetic properties of a bcc phase which surrounds the main Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l4</inf>B phase in the material, and the appearance of reverse domains at crystal surfaces, grain boundaries and phase interfaces. The bcc phase, induced by annealing from the amorphous state, was found to have soft magnetic properties compared with the main phase. Formation of Nd and Tb layers on clean Nd-Fe-B surfaces resulted in greatly increased coercivity, indicating that the states of crystal surfaces and grain boundaries are indeed important in determining the coercive force.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Zn Alloys Produced by Vapor Quenching
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: X-ray diffraction, magnetization and Mössbauer effect have been measured for vapor quenched Fe-Zn alloys. The single bcc alloys are obtained for the Zn concentration between 0 and 60 at%. They are ferromagnetic at room temperature and their magnetic moment decreases with the increase in Zn concentration, slightly deviating upwards from the simple dilution law. The broad resonance line of Mössbauer spectrum indicates the wide distribution of hyperfine fields of these alloys.

abstract: Impurity gases during sputtering can have serious effects on magnetic properties of a Co-Cr perpendicular recording medium. articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Property of CoFeCr Sputtered Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The dependence of magnetic properties of CoFeCr films on film composition and the effects of heat treatment are discussed. Saturation magnetization started decreasing when the Cr concentration was increased to 40 at% and reached zero at 58 at%. articleTitle: Effect of Domain Structure of Main Pole Film on Reproducing Sensitivity of SPT Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The domain structures of narrow-track single-pole heads for perpendicular magnetic recording have been observed, and their effects on the reproducing sensitivities were investigated. The ratio of the double height 2h of the closure domain to the track width W increases when the track width and the anisotropy field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> of a Co-Zr-Nb amorphous main pole film decrease. The maximum reproducing sensitivity for each narrow-track head is obtained for the optimum value of Hk, when the ratio of 2h to W is about 30 percent. When the Hk is smaller than the optimum value giving the maximum sensitivity, the reproduced voltage not only decreases but is also unstable, changing with every cycle of recording. On the other hand, the reproduced voltage is stable, and becomes smaller for larger values of Hk, because the permeability of the film decreases. The reproducing sensitivity of the narrow track single pole head, formed from film having the optimum H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> value, does not decrease even for heads with tracks 10 micron wide.

articleTitle: Amorphous Alloy Cores for Switching Regulator

abstract: Amorphous alloy applications for various magnetic devices have been investigated. This review discusses application of amorphous alloys in the magnetic cores of switching regulators, including magnetic amplifiers, spike killers, choke coils, and main transformers. Amorphous alloys are shown to be useful in raising performances and reducing the sizes of switching regulators.

articleTitle: Compositional Microstructure of Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The microcolumnar structure of Co-Cr film has been studied using chemical etching. Only the columns are dissolved, leaving the column boundaries with a micro-honeycomb structure. From compositional analysis of the etchant after etching, Cr segregated column boundaries have been confirmed to exist even in Co-Cr films sputtered at high sputtering rates. Co-Cr films with higher Hc show sharper and narrower grain boundaries of a higher Cr content. It is concluded that the degree of Cr segregation is a very important factor in the control of the magnetic properties of Co-Cr films.

articleTitle: Effects of Additive Elements on Corrosion Resistance of RE-TM Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Rare earth-transition metal amorphous films are promising for use in erasable optical memory media. However, they have the drawback of poor reliability due to poor corrosion resistance. Corrosion of films is classified as either surface oxidation, selective oxidation of RE metals, or pitting corrosion. We have studied the corrosion behavior and succeeded in improving the corrosion resistance. To raise the latter, one of the elements Co, Ni, Pt, Al, Cr, or Ti was added to Tb-Fe and Tb-Co films by simultaneous sputtering. The films (no protection) were subjected to an accelerated aging test. The elements were classified into two groups, Co, Ni, and Pt, on the one hand, Al, Cr, and Ti, on the other. Elements in the former group are only effective in preventing surface oxidation and pitting corrosion. The latter group of elements, however, is effective in inhibiting corrosion in all of the above modes. This high corrosion resistance can be explained in terms of the elements' ability to bind oxygen and to form passive states. The elements are effective in improving corrosion resistance in the order Cr, Ti, Al. These additives cause no appreciable change in the magneto-optical properties.

articleTitle: Polarity Reversal of Hall Voltage at Compensation Temperature in Amorphous RE-Ni (RE:Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho) Films with Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy

abstract: Various amorphous rare earth - Ni (ferrimagnetic) films were prepared, and the temperature dependences of their Hall loops studied, to elucidate the mechanism by which the Hall polarity is suddenly reversed at the compensation temperature T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">comp</sub>. At temperatures below T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">comp</sub>, where the Gd spin dominates, ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub> ≫ 0, lending support to the hypothesis that the transition metal spin plays a dominant role in the Hall effect mechanism in RE-TM films.

articleTitle: Effect of Tartronic Acid on Magnetic Properties of Electroless Plated Co-Ni-Re-P Alloy Films for a Perpendicular Recording Medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Electroless plated Co-Ni-Re-P alloy films for use as perpendicular magnetic recording media were studied. It was found that the addition of tartronic acid to the plating bath makes it possible to form Co-Ni-Re-P perpendicular anisotropic films with no MnSO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> present. Co-Ni-Re-P alloy films, with a composition simpler than that of previously developed Co-Ni-Re-Mn-P films, has a greater potential than do the latter for practical use as perpendicular recording media. The read/write characteristics of 8-inch disks employing Co-Ni-Re-P films were also measured, in combination with a ring head. Characteristics almost equal to those of media containing Mn were obtained, and even higher recording densities are expected, given improved matching of head and disk properties. A recording density of D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> = 54 kFRPI was obtained for a 0.2 micron thick medium, using a 0.33 micron gap ring head and with a 0.12 micron head-medium spacing.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Ce Amorphous Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Crystalline Ce alloys often exhibit properties which are different from other rare-earth alloys. We wanted to know if a similar tendency was present in amorphous phase Ce alloys. The magnetic properties of such alloys were compared with the results of other rare-earth alloys. The concentration dependence of the Curie temperature of Fe-Ce alloys is similar to that of Fe-Zr and Fe-Ti amorphous alloys. Such properties suggest that Ce is a tretavalent element in Fe-Ce alloys. There is no significant difference in the resistivity of the various alloys used.

articleTitle: Domain Wall and Domain Structure of Amorphous Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Studies on the effects of nonmagnetic (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) intermediate layers of various thicknesses in amorphous Co-Zr-Nb films are described. articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Transition Metal Nitride--Synthesis of Iron Nitride by High-Dose Nitrogen Ion Implantation--

abstract: Nitrogen ions (N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) were implanted into pure iron films in an attempt to produce Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and other iron nitride phases. Ions were implanted at 150 keV and dosages were ranged from 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> to 2.11 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup> ions/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and magnetization measurements and X-ray diffraction studies performed. Ferromagnetic Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N and Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>N phases were found intermixed with the α-Fe, but there was no evidence of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. The saturation magnetization decreased slowly with increasing dosage, but dropped abruptly by 40 percent at the highest dose, due to the formation of a paramagnetic Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>N phase. articleTitle: Magnetoresistive Effect of Vacuum Evaporated Ni-Co Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Because of the large anisotropic magnetic field of Ni-Co films, there have been few reports on their magnetoresistive effect. The authors succeeded in vacuum evaporation of Ni-Co (Ni content 60 - 85 percent) films with a small anisotropic magnetic field, and studied the resulting magnetic properties. The magnetoresistive effect was largest for 77 percent Ni-Co, at approximately 5 percent, but when the substrate temperature was varied no change in the magnetoresistive effect was seen for temperatures above 250°C. A Ni-Fe film was placed next to Ni-Co film formed under optimum conditions, to obtain better low magnetic field sensitivity than is possible with Ni-Fe alone. Also, the Ni-Co had a nearly single domain structure, with stable magnetization.

The magnetization of alloys with a higher La concentration saturated more easily, but for low concentration alloys, there was a more pronounced curve and no saturation in the magnetization curves. The Fe-La alloys have a high-field susceptibility that is much larger than Co-base alloys, and is similar to Invar alloys. publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors describe apparatus for the highly accurate measurement of stray magnetic fields in a modification of Pfützner's method, and discuss the relation between the stray field distribution and basic 180° domains in (100), [001] 3 percent Si-Fe single-crystal sheets. A GaAs Hall element connected to a precision positioning device was used to detect normal field components on the sheet surface. The positions of Bloch walls, as determined by mapping from field measurements, agreed well with the positions from domain pattern photographs. The field was found to be greatest at the centers of domains, and the effect of scratching in reducing the stray field was also studied.

articleTitle: Write ard Read Characteristics in Combination with a Single Pole Type Thin Film Head and a Double Layer Rigid Disk for Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A single-pole type thin-film head for perpendicular magnetic recording was developed, and the effects of head and disk parameters were studied. The newly developed single pole head consists of an amorphous Co-Zr main pole and a coil of 16 turns. Poles are tapered at the tip end, and range from 0.2 to 0.5 micron in thickness and from 2 to 15 microns in depth. First, the effects of the pole thickness and pole depth on write and read performance of the head were investigated. A Co-Cr/permalloy double layer rigid disk was used for evaluation. The thickness of the Co-Cr layer is 0.14 micron, and that of the permalloy packing layer is 0.5 micron. Perpendicular coercivity of the Co-Cr layer is 730 Oe. The recording density increased as the pole thickness decreased, and a D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> of 70 kFRPI was achieved for a head with a 0.2-micron pole thickness. Isolated output was 0.53 μVp-p/micron/ turn at a disk speed of 6 m/s. The magnetomotive force required for saturation recording was as low as 0.19 AT. It was found that there is very little influence of the pole depth on the write and read performance. The effects of perpendicular coercivity and film thickness of the double layer disk on the recording characteristics were examined. The recording density and write sensitivity were improved as the thickness of the Co-Cr layer decreased. The output voltage increased with the perpendicular coercivity.

abstract: To clarify the origin of rotatable anisotropy observed in CoZr sputtered films, the effects of Ar pressure and other conditions during RF sputtering of samples on glass were studied. abstract: A new method for observing domain and other microstructure features of films by detecting secondary electron spins is described. articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Permalloy Films By High-Rate Triode Sputtering

abstract: Permalloy film was formed by triode sputtering and vacuum-annealed in a magnetic field (150 Oe), and changes in magnetic properties induced by the annealing were studied. abstract: A parametric magnetic sensor was used to develop a clamp-type ammeter capable of measuring low currents in the range from dc to high frequencies. The principle of operation is described, and results for the output of a prototype device are presented. The frequency characteristic was flat from dc to a few hundred Hz. The range of measurable currents may be adjusted by appropriate design of the magnetic core and the number of core windings.

articleTitle: On Propagation Properties of Lamb-Type and SH-Type Magnetoelastic Waves in Highly Magnetostrictive Slab
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: While most studies of magnetoelastic waves (MEWs) have dealt with very thin samples, the sample thickness becomes important for Lamb and SH type MEWs. Theoretical and experimental studies on MEW propagation in an infinitely extended slab are reported. Matrix and eigenvalue methods were used in theoretical calculations, while METGLAS 2605CO and 2605S2 samples were employed in experiments. Both calculations and experiments indicated the existence of three fundamental MEW modes, (P + SV) -type flexxural (MEW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sup>) and SH-type (MEW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>). Whereas the velocity for MEW f-type waves decreased with frequency, agreeing qualitatively with the results of Tsuya et al., the velocity for MEWs tended to increase, a behavior which may be useful for realizing large changes in MEW velocity at high frequencies.

articleTitle: A New Type of Magneto-Optic Readout Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A "domain-modulation-type optical reproduction head" is reported, in which the signal field is transmitted through a high permeability film to a readout magnetic film, which enlarges the domain and enables reproduction by laser light. Magnetic garnet was used as the readout film, and (60 to 300 μm thick) Permalloy as the high permeability film. In tests, the modulated domain width of the garnet was greater (approximately 4 μm) than for the Permalloy, suggesting the possibility for high-resolution laser reproduction.

articleTitle: Flux Control Characteristic of Open and Closed FOC
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors succeeded in controlling the flux in ferrite orthogonal cores (FOC) by raising them out of or lowering them into a magnetic fluid. Several differences between open and closed FOCs were observed: 1) when submerged, open type FOCs and the magnetic fluid form a serial magnetic circuit, while the closed type forms a parallel magnetic circuit; 2) the main magnetic flux in the core of open FOCs can be controlled directly, while the closed type controls only leakage flux; 3) the flux can be controlled in both body and legs of the open type, but only in the legs of the closed type; and 4) the open type is more sensitive to such control.

articleTitle: Compact Magneto-Optical Disk for Coded Data Storage
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A compact magneto-optical disk drive compatible with current optical disk systems is reported. A tracking detection system enabling use with add-on (non-erasable) optical disks was adopted. High-speed accessing was accomplished by constructing the head from both stationary and moving mechanisms. Noise analyses showed that for large analyzer angles θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub>, N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">disk</sub> ≫ N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">laser</sub> ≫ N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">shot</sub>, but when the SN ratio was maximum at θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub> ~ 10°, the three noise levels were roughly equal.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan

articleTitle: Effects of Substrate Bias on the Structrue and Magnetic Properties Of Sputtered TbFe Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The substrate bias voltage and Ar pressure were varied during RF diode sputtering of TbFe films, to study the influence of these parameters on the film perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. Ar pressures were 10 and 30 mTorr, and bias voltages ranged from 0 to -350 V. Depending on both the Ar pressure and bias voltage, film structures varied from coarse to fine, with columnar structures appearing and disappearing, and the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> value was related to the microstructure. Attempts were made to explain these dependences.

articleTitle: Micro-Structure and Magnetic Properties of Perpendicular Magnetized Co-CoO Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The electrical resistivity of reactive RF sputtered Co-CoO films increases and the temperature coefficient of resistivity decreases with the formation of CoO. For films with a saturation magnetization (M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) of more than 670 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the resistivity decreases irreversibly above 370 K by deoxidization. For films with an M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> of less than 470 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the resistivity increases irreversibly above 420 K. After the irreversible increase in resistivity, the coercivity (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) and squareness ratio of the hysteresis loop perpendicular to the film plane increase, and the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> parallel to the film plane decreases.

articleTitle: Analysis and Improvement of Measuring Method of Magnetic Fields in Single Sheet Testers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Leakage flux tends to disturb the magnetic field near the H coil in single sheet testers during measurements of high-permeability materials. The authors propose an improved sheet measurement method using two H coils, situated at different distances from the high-permeability material. The field strength in the two coils are measured, and extrapolation to a distance L = 0 is used to obtain the true strength. For high-permeability materials, the measurement accuracy is thus improved greatly over that of the conventional H coil method.

articleTitle: NMR of MnAl and MnBi1-xSbx
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: NMR studies of MnAl and MnBiSb magnetic materials are reported. Mn samples were prepared by melting, quenching and heat treating for 30 min at 500°C. Satellite lines attributed to <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">55</sup>Mn resonance with Mn atoms in Al nearest-neighbor sites was also observed; a similar <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">27</sup>Al satellite line was also observed. The Mn atoms in Al sites had magnetic moments antiparallel to the regular Mn atoms, a result confirmed by neutron diffraction studies. For MnBi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">55</sup>Mn NMR lines were observed at around x = 0.02 but not at x = 0.05.

articleTitle: Properties of FeAl Soft Magnetic Thin Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties of FeAl alloy films, deposited by evaporation in a magnetic field, were studied to explore the possibility of their use in place of Permalloy in thin film recording heads. For Al concentrations of 20 to 30 at% or less, M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> values were large compared with those for Permalloy. Resistivity increased monotonically with Al concentration, while the hardness reached a maximum of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> = 1300 at 11 at% Al. It is concluded that such FeAl films may serve in place of Permalloy in thin-film heads.

The relation between closure domains in Co-Zr-Nb amorphous main-pole films and the reproduction sensitivity of the head was studied. It was found that for narrow track widths and low film H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> values, the proportion of closure domains increases, and reproduction sensitivities fall off. articleTitle: Shape Stability of Magnetic Fluid
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A study of the instability of a spheroidal droplet of magnetic fluid in a uniform magnetic field, without a gravitational field, is described. A droplet of ferrofluid was suspended in water or glycerin, the droplet minor axis was measured for fields up to 1.2 kOe, and the interfacial tension between the ferrofluid and the water or glycerin was determined. The ratio of the droplet major axis to the minor axis K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> increased with increasing field, and depended on the initial droplet diameter. The results could be explained by minimizing the sum of the magnetic energy and the surface energy with respect to K.

articleTitle: Interaction Between Vertical Bloch Line and In-Plane Field
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An in-plaane magnetic field, generated by a conductor pattern, is used to propagate Bloch line pairs, and to execute pair separation and recoupling processes. A row of parallel condcuctor stripes is connected to form two series, and the series are driven by a current pulse phase-shifted 1/4 cycle, to drive BL pairs. Pair separation and recoupling is effected by appropriately modifying the connections of the stripe conductors and the phase shift between drivirng currents. The results are applicable to gate operation in Bloch line memories.

articleTitle: Iron Thin Films by Means of Dual Ion-Beam Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Dual ion-beam sputtering from high-purity targets was used to form iron thin films with improved magnetic and chemical properties. Films obtained were amorphous according to X-ray diffraction studies, and while H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> increased for ion accelerating voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sg</sub> above 140 V, 4πMs first increased with increasing V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sg</sub> and then fell off. Normal hysteresis loops were obtained for films formed with V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sg</sub> = 0 to 115 V, but films formed at 155 V had rotational hysteresis loops. By controlling the energy of ions deposited on the surface, it was possible to form films with a high 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> (20 kG) and low H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> (1.4 Oe); ion deposition also tended to make film compositions uniform and improve the atomic ordering.

articleTitle: Film Growth and Magnetization Reversal Mechanism of Co-Cr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new method of evaluating the magnetization reversal mechanism is used for both single- and double-layer Co-Cr films. The mechanism for thick films is by rotation and for thin films it is by domain wall motion. The mechanism for any given film is evaluated by angular dependence of the hysteresis loss and coercive force for the films of thickness above 380 Å, the magnetization reversal mechanism takes place by rotation. At 250 Å, the film shows the tendencies of the magnetization reversal by domain wall motion. The investigation has suggested the pseudo double-layer structure with respect to the magnetization mechanism in single-layer films.

The temperature dependence of the electrical resistivity in the range 10 to 300K was discussed for the respective group alloys. Only the data for group 5) metallic glasses can be consistently interpreted on the basis of the generalized Faber-Ziman theory. Nevertheless, it was shown that the 2k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>/K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>=l.0 criterion is not sufficient to predict a negative TCR even in group 5) alloys.

articleTitle: Combustion Processes Under Intense Magentic Fields
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: As a means of clarifying the effect of dc magnetic fields on oxidation reactions in living organisms, the authors studied combustion phenomena in air. In one experiment, benzine was injected into four Pt body warmers, which were ignited with two exposed to a graded dc magnetic field (1.0 T, 10 T/m); the combustion time of the exposed group was 16 percesnt shorter on average. In another experiment, two body warmers were placed at the poles of an electromagnet and ignited, and combustion times measured, turning the magnet on and off; combustion times were 15.6 percent shorter on average when exposed to the field.

articleTitle: The Structure of Metal Evaporated Tape
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To investigate the structure of evaporated tapes used in magnetic recording, and particularly the possible presence of a surface oxide layer, several tape samples were fabricated by oxygen reaction oblique-incidence evaporation, varying the amount of reacting oxygen, and analyzed the sample structures by XPS, AES, and X-ray diffraction. It was found that the region near the surface is a mixed phase of metal atoms and oxides. These oxides changed from CoO to Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>+CoO, and then to Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, as the amount of oxygen was increased. However, intermixing of CoO with metal atoms is thought to contribute to the film durability.

articleTitle: Spatial Resolution Improvement of Spin-Polarized Scanning Electron Microscope
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A previously developed method of magnetic domain observation which relies on detection of the spin polariization of secondary electrons emitted from the sample surface during scanning with a primary electron beam, and on converting the spin polarization into an image signal, has been further developed. Specifically, the efficiency of the spin detector used was raised, and an electron gun with a narrower primary electron beam adopted to improve spatial resolution to approximately 0.2 μm. Images obtained using the method for polycrystalline Fe are presented; ten minutes were required to obtain a single image.

articleTitle: Current Density Dependence of Magnetoresistive Effect in NiFe Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: NiFe film samples with positive, negative and zero-valued magnetostrictions were formed by EB evaporation on quartz and BK-7 glass substrates, and the current density dependence of the MR effect was investigated. articleTitle: Observation of Magnetic Fields in the Scanning Electron Microscope
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: It is shown that SEM secondary electron images and reproduced waveforms of recorded bit patterns differ for perpendicular and in-plane magnetization films. Using Co-Cr/Ni-Fe double-layer films and VTR metal tape as perpendicular and in-plane magnetization films, it was found that the magnetic flux becomes horizontal in the magnetization transition and the recording regions, respectively. It was concluded that magnetic contrast is generated in response to the magnetization transition region for Co-Cr/Ni-Fe film, and to the recording region for VTR tape. The reproduced waveforms are dependent on the horizontal component of the leakage field; the waveforms are triangular for perpendicular magnetization films, and trapezoidal for in-plane films.

articleTitle: Preparation and Properties of Colloidal Ferromagnetic Metals
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Preparation of Co and Fe ferromagnetic colloids using a mixture of oil-soluble surfactants and a saturated hydrocarbon oil is described. Amines with long-chain lipophilic alkyl radicals and sulfonates were used as the surfactants, and a drum was rotated to draw the liquid into a film while evaporating the metal in vacuum, gradually increasing the colloid concentration in the liquid. Monodisperse colloidal particles of uniform size (about 50 Å) were obtained. Co colloids formed in this way were super-paramagnetic at 246 K and above, and the colloidal particle concentration was 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> to 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup>. articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetization Distribution in Magnetic Film Edge
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To analyze the magnetostatic energy near the edge of a magnetic thin film under an external field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>, a parabolic function was assumed to describe the magnetization distribution in the edge region. The result was then used in minimizing the total energy to analyze the curling state near the film edge. It was found that for low applied fields, the magnetic moments near the edge are aligned almost parallel to the edge, and the curling length is long (approx. 100 μm); whereas for stronger fields (in excess of 100 Oe), the moments tend toward a perpendicular alignment and the curling length decreases, and at the same time volume magnetic charge is converted into surface charge.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Highly Sensitive Magnetoresistive Sensors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A barber-pole type magnetoresistive sensor with excellent sensitivity and temperature characteristics is described. 76 wt% Ni-Fe layers 480 Å and 1030 Å thick were vapor deposited with a TaMo adhesive layer and Au patterning; magnetic field annealing was used to induce uniaxial anisotropy. Output characteristics were reproducible to within 1 percent, with minimal hysteresis effects; the average sensitivity was 0.13 mV/Oe·mA, comparable to that of InSb Hall sensors, while the output temperature coefficient was -0.09 %/°C, superior to InSb devices. The test device was used to read data from a magnetic card, with good results.

articleTitle: Generation and Propagation of Magnetoelastic Wave in Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The generation of magnetoelastic waves in the 10 GHz band, through the application of parallel RF and DC magnetic fields at the surface of a highly magnetostrictive ferromagnetic sample is reported. Excitation and detection cavities were used to generate and detect magntoelastic waves. The magnetic field dependences of signals from both cavities were measured, and propagation characteristics were determined by the pulse transmission method, for both the H⫽,⫽ and the H⫽,⊥ modes. Using a Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">78</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> amorphous film sample, a transmitted signal was detected near the resonance field, propagating in the H⫽,⫽ mode at 4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> m/s, which corresponds to an elastic wave. The nature of the phenomenon is as yet unclear.

articleTitle: A Numerical Method for Three Phase Transformer Circuits Using the Tableau Form
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The tableau form is applied in nonlinear analysis of bank connection three-phase transformer circuits. Differences between bank connection transformers and three-phase circuits using three-phase iron cores appear only in the magnetic circuit, and not in the electrical system. Numerical analysis of the Y-Y connection indicated the generation of a neutral point voltage, which originates in the nonlinearity of the iron core. In a linear analysis, this neutral point voltage did not appear at any applied voltage.

articleTitle: Elastic Properties of Nd2Fe14B Between 120 and 300 K
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors conducted elasticity and specific heat measurements of Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B compounds, used in permanent magnets, to investigate the mechanism of a change in the easy magnetization axis direction at 130 K. Neither the elasticity nor the rigidity showed a notable temperature dependence, in contrast to certain rare earth-iron compounds, in which the elasticity drops sharply. The specific heat showed little temperature dependence below 180 K, and no sharp peak was observed, in contrast to the observation of a sharp peak accompanying rotation of the easy magnetization axis in PrCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>.

articleTitle: Extraordinary Oscillation in Nonlinear Polyphase Circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Polyphase circuit phenomena are discussed from the standpoint of improving reliability of conversion detection devices used in measuring equipment. A nonlinear three-phase circuit was analyzed by the harmonic balance method. It was found that the line impedance Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> and line resistance R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> have a very large effect on the zero phase voltage and extraordinary oscillation region, and that the line and protective relay load capacitances C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</inf> are closely related to the skip phenomenon.

articleTitle: Numerical Stability of Lumped Constant Model for VBL Dynamics
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An implicit method is used to improve the stability of the numerical simulation of vertical Bloch line motion. In the equations of motion, V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub>, V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sub> and ϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> are replaced by their respective changes per time increment ΔT. The values of the various force terms at a future time T + ΔT are estimated from their values at time T using appropriate correction terms, and a system of simultaneous linear equations in ΔR, Δϕa and ΔS is obtained for each domain wall point. Whereas explicit solutions are numerically stable for ΔT as large as 0.2 ns, this implicit solution is stable for ΔT taken as large as 16 ns.

articleTitle: Stability of Ba-Ferrite Magnetic Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An endurance test was performed on a 3.5-inch floppy disk media of particulate Ba-ferrite film at room temperature under normal humidity conditions. Head contact was established more than 10 million times without any reduction in output being exhibited, demonstrating that this is a media with very good endurance and stable characteristics. Ba-ferrite media exhibit small pressure demagnetization and stable endurance with respect to temperature variation, confirming that it is an excellent material for magnetic recording media.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Although progress has been made in clarifying the details of magnetization processes in MnZnFe ternary ferrite single crystals at room temperature, little is known of the temperature dependences of crystal properties. The changes with temperature (liquid nitrogen to 300 K) in magnetostriction in the ≪100≫ and ≪111≫ directions, in the initial permeability, and in the magnetic anisotropy constants K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Contrary to expectations, however, the value of K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> was not the only factor related to the initial permeability maximum, and a simple explanation of the temperature characteristics in terms of anisotropy alone is not possible.

articleTitle: Substitution of Mn for Cr in Crystalline and Amorphous CrrGe
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The substitution of Mn for Cr in crystalline CrGe compounds can change the magnetic characteristics from paramagnetic to ferromagnetic to spin glass, but the same substitution in amorphous CrGe causes a change from paramagnetic to spin glass with no discernable ferromagnetic phase. This difference is believed to be due to the difference in the magnetic polarization of Mn. The freezing temperature rose with increases in Mn while μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> shows almost no compositional dependence. The magnetic susceptibility of these compounds followed the Curie-Weiss law.

articleTitle: Impedance of Magnetic Coaxial Pipe
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: It was found that a coaxial pipe consisting of two ferromagnetic pipes exhibits interesting properties, as the skin effect is considerable even at low frequencies when current is passed in the pipes. Among other results, it was found that the impedances of the inner and outer pipes Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</inf> and Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">out</inf> were considerably different, and that there exists a current frequency at which Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">out</inf> is minimum. A qualitative vector diagram and quantitative formulae are presented relating the impedances to the current densities and magnetic fluxes in the pipes.

articleTitle: Propagation of Surface Magnetoelastic Waves in Sputtered Fe-Co-B Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Propagation of surface magnetoelastic waves (SMEWs) at high frequencies (up to 50 MHz) in Fe-Co-B amorphous film formed by RF sputtering onto glass and silicon wafer substrates are described. Piezoelectric transducers were used for SMEW excitation and detection. Output signals showed that, as expected, of the (P+SV)-L, SH, and (P+SV)-T waves, only the latter changes velocity noticeably with the field. The velocity was found to change by a maximum 2.8 percent when a 60 Oe field was applied; however, magnetic annealing had no great effect on this change. The field had a drastic effect on the SH wave amplitude, attributed to the close coupling of the substrate SAW with the metallic magnetic film.

articleTitle: Switching Regulator Controlled by High-Frequency Magnetic Amplifier
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The operation of a push-pull converter constructed using a self-excited inverter (a multivibrator) is described. While the switching losses of FETs in the inverter were small, turn-on and turn-off slopes changed depending on the load conditions, so that the oscillating frequency varied slightly. Two types of magnetic cores were used in experiments; power conversion efficiencies reached 76 percent or more for load currents from 5 to 10 A, and the oscillating frequency changed by about 10 percent in the 0 to 10 A range. Use of a core with good frequency characteristics should enable operation at up to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Structure and Characteristics of Wire Inductor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Flexible amorphous metal fibers were woven with copper wire to form inductor, which were smaller and had a higher inductance than conventional toroidal magnetic cores. The amorphous wire, commercially available, was 107 μm in diameter, with a zero-magnetostriction composition; the copper wire had a 140 μm diameter. One such element had an inductance of 3 μH/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The inductance frequency characteristic was flat, and by changing the construction of the element, the frequency at which the Q-factor is maximum may be varied.

articleTitle: A New Magneto-Optic Transfer Readout with Magnetic Garnet Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Previous garnet film transfer readout methods suffered from drawbacks such as transfer domain disorder and slow response. Here a new type of transfer readout method, in which the domains of garnet film are formed into parallel stripes and the garnet film is placed close to the recording medium, so that leakage flux from the latter changes the garnet domain widths, which are detected by a laser readout beam. In experiments, signals recorded at 5 MHz and various recording currents were read out as expected, with transfer domains changing continuously with the recording current. The new method seems to be feasible for use in high-speed response narrow-track readout.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To throw light on the factors influencing the coercivity of Nd-Fe-B system magnets, the authors studied the effect of annealing on the material coercive force. Sintering at l00°C and aging at 6OO-650°C and at 900°C were found to increase the coercivity greatly; this was thought to arise from formation of minute Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B crystals upon sintering, and partial elimination of lattice defects at grain surfaces and within grains upon aging.

articleTitle: Switching Characteristics and Applications of Amorphous CT Core Pulse Triggered Power Transistors (PTPT)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: High-speed switching in bipolar-type pulse-triggered power transistors using an ultra-small nonmagnetostrictive amorphous core were reported. High-speed turn-on and turn-off operation was obtained by raising the self-oscillation frequency to 380 kHz. The electrical loss versus switching frequency characteristic was determined, and a large safe operating area was verified. Potential applications of such PTPTs are as power transistors and in inverters and static switches.

articleTitle: Thermal Stability of Nonequilibrium Fe-Ag and Fe-Cu Alloys Produced by Vapor Quenching
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: X-ray diffraction and Mössbauer effect measurements were carried out for sputtered fcc Fe-Ag and Fe-Cu alloys after being annealed at various temperatures. At temperatures higher than 300°C, the metastable fcc phase decomposes by removing supersaturated Fe atoms. In the fcc Fe-Ag alloys, Fe atoms always give a ferromagnetic hyperfine field component during the clustering process. On the other hand, in the fcc Fe-Cu alloys, the supersaturated Fe atoms form clusters and behave as γ-Fe, giving a small, hyperfine field component.

articleTitle: Depositions of Co-Cr Films by EP magnetron Sputtering Technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fast Co-Cr film deposition speed was obtained using the exposed pole (EP) magnetron sputtering technique. At an Ar gas pressure of 0.2 Pa and an applied power density of 7.6 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, a maximum film deposition speed of 0.18 μm/min was obtained. It was found that the film thickness and Co content both decrease monotonically from the center of the substrate outwards. Film thickness and Co content were found to be optimal under low Ar gas pressure and low magnetic field induced by the solenoid coil (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>).

articleTitle: The Problems in the Development of Magneto-Optical Devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The problems to be solved in the development of future magneto-optical devices are described. Iron garnets, especially bismuth substituted iron garnets, are promising for magneto-optical materials in the 0.8 μm and 1.l-1.6 μm wavelength ranges. However, further improvement of the figure of merit and crystal growth technique is fundamental to realizing high-quality, compact and low-cost devices. With the advance of visible laser diodes, a new class of magneto-optical materials such as CdMnTe will be required for the shorter wavelength region. For waveguide devices, it seems important to develop various basic technologies, such as TE-TM mode phase matching, control of ofmagnetization direction, and fabrication of nonreciprocal and reciprocal pats in a film. Lastly, the problems in thin film integrated optical devices based on Bragg diffraction of guided light by magnetostatic surface waves are briefly described.

articleTitle: 1985 Index - IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan, Vol. TJMJ-1
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This index covers all items-papers, correspondence, reviews, etc.-that appeared in this periodical during 1985. The index is divided into an Author Index and a Subject Index, both arranged alphabetically. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item; this entry is listed under the name of the first author and includes coauthor names, title, location of the item, and notice of corrections and comments if any. Crossreferences are given from each coauthor name to the name of the corresponding first author. The location of the item is specified by the journal name (abbreviated), year, month, and inclusive pages. The Subject Index contains several entries for each item, each consisting of a subject heading, modifying phrase(s), first author's name-followed by + if the paper has coauthors-and enough information to locate the item. For coauthors, title, comments, and corrections if any, etc., it is necessary to refer to the primary entry in the Author Index. Subject cross-references are provided as required by the subject matter. Also provided whenever appropriate are listings under generic headings such as Bibliographies (for any paper with at least 50 references, as well as papers that are exclusively bibliographies), Bookreviews, and Special issues.

articleTitle: Stripe Domain Stabilization for Bloch Line Memory
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Ring-shaped domains, consisting of an inner and an outer domain wall, were studied as a means of achieving stable domains in Bloch line memories. Grooves were formed in a (YSmLuCa)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(FeGe)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1 2</inf> film on GGG substrate by ion milling, and various characteristics, such as the range of bias fields allowing domain stability for various plateau widths, were investigated. The proposed method was found to meet the conditions required for domain stability, and to enable conversion of VBL pairs into bubbles; as one drawback, however, this arrangement may make it difficult to achieve high track densities.

articleTitle: Magnetic Characteristics of CoZrNb Amorphous Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Methods for controlling the coercive force and anisotropic magnetic field of amorphous CoZrNb thin films are reported. Films were RF-sputtered onto glass and ceramic substrates, the latter mirror-polished in directions differing by 90°. Films formed on the ceramic substrates had H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> fields in preferred directions, while samples formed on glass showed no such directional preference for H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>. Films were then annealed in static and rotating magnetic fields; it was found that the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> of as-sputtered films may be realigned by static field annealing, while the strength of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> may be regulated by a combination of static- and rotating-field annealing.

articleTitle: Generation and Detection of Magnetoelastic Waves in Magnetic Thin Films Using Planar Coils
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: While many magnetoelastic wave (MEW) devices employ piezoelectric methods for wave generation, the authors demonstrate the feasibility of generating and detecting MEWs using a pair of planar coils. An Fe-Si-B magnetic film sputtered onto glass was used; waves were found to propagate in both the magnetic film and the glass. For the film with an MEW velocity of 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> km/s and coil pitch of 1 mm, the detection output should be strongest at multiples and fractions of the 5 MHz fundamental, and in fact output peaks were observed at 1.3, 1.7, and 2.5 MHz.

articleTitle: Mössbauer Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Applications of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">57</sup>Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy to the study of ferromagnetic amorphous alloys are discussed. Typical Mössbauer spectra of the amorphous Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">83</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub> alloy were compared with those obtained from ordered and disordered crystalline ferromagnets, Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Si, which show distinct hyperfine fields depending on the atomic environments in the lattice. Thermal scanning was applied to determine the Curie temperature of amorphous ferromagnets and proved to be useful. Conversion electron Mössbauer spectroscopy (CEMS) makes it possible to study the surface states of the amorphous alloys. Simultaneous measurements of scattering and transmission Mössbauer spectra are presented using the work performed for amorphous Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">83</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> alloy. abstract: Experiments were described in which a plastic sphere was filled with saline solution and an ac current run through the solution, to simulate magnetic fields in the vicinity of the human brain, such as are observed by magnetoencephalogram (MEG) topography. abstract: In recent years, the growth of switched-mode power supply production has been truly remarkable. abstract: In addition to the usual lumped constant model for vertical Bloch lines, the authors introduce exchange repulsive forces acting between VBL, and processing to describe passing of normal domain wall points by VBL. Assumptions regarding ϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> and δϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> are made for BL winding in the positive and negative directions, and an empirical formula for the repulsive force in terms of the VBL separation is derived from distributed VBL model simulations. The passing processing assumes normal domain wall points approached by VBL points to vanish, while at the same time new wall points are generated behind the VBL point.

articleTitle: A Coercivity Measuring Method of Barium Ferrote Fome Powder for Particulate Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A Barium ferrite platelet fine particle coercive force is affected by magnetic particle agglomeration. Investigations of a new measuring method to determine the intrinsic coercive force of Ba-ferrite particles that exclude the effect of magnetic agglomeration are reported. The new method was to make coercive force measurements for Ba-ferrite particles dispersed and attached on large SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> particle surfaces. Coercive force measurement for samples of low Ba-ferrite/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixing ratio confirmed that it was possible to measure the intrinsic coercive force excluding the influence of magnetic agglomeration.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetostriction on External Load by Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To better understand vibration phenomena in transformers, analysis of magnetostriction in stressed materials was conducted using the finite element method. Starting with functionals for the total elastic and magnetic field energies, a one-dimensional approximating expression for the magnetostriction was derived, using experimental values for the magnetostriction-flux density curve in the unstressed state. Experiments verified the reasonableness of the expression obtained; further, analysis of the magnetostriction is possible for non-uniform stresses as well.

articleTitle: DC-To-DC Converter with GTO Controlled by Extremely Small Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A low power-loss, highly reliable dc-dc converter was constructed which employs an ultra-small saturable magnetic core in the GTO (gate-turn-off) thyristor gate circuit. The circuit configuration is given and its operation explained. The GTO on/off ratio is easily regulated through the reset magnetic flux by a low controlling voltage. At outputs of 1 kW or more, an efficiency of 90 percent is achieved; another feature of the circuit is its small number of components. Research to apply the same circuit in high-power high-frequency applications is underway.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Expression of Retentivity in Electromagnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An electric equivalent circuit was derived from measurements of the retentivity decay characteristics of electromagnets (solenoids), and the relationship between spring strength and oscillation-free magnetizing currents was studied. Several time constants related to the decay were in evidence; two of these could be determined with precision, allowing formulation of an equivalent circuit with two RC loops in series. The R and C values in these loops are related to the solenoid attractive force, shape, material used, temperature, and surface contact area.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Study on Hybrid Magnetic Bubble Memory Using 0.5 μm Diameter Magnetic Bubbles
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To develop a hybrid magnetic bubble memory with a storage density of 16 Mb/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> or more, an investigation is being made into the properties of ion-implanted propagation tracks with bubbles of 0.5 μm in diameter and permalloy propagation tracks. This article reports on the adjustment of operating bias magnetic fields in ion-implanted and permalloy propagation tracks, as well as the characteristics of permalloy tracks at extended periods (4 - 20 μm).

articleTitle: Wall Observations in Fe77Nd15B8 Sintered Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors report electron microscopic studies of domain wall pinning at grain boundaries in Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">77</inf>Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> sintered magnets. A wall was observed to be strongly pinned at a triple junction of grain boundaries, in what was determined to be ferromagnetic bcc phase material. This agrees with Hiraga et al's suggestion that bcc phase boundary regions are closely related to the magnetic properties of the material.

articleTitle: Operating Characteristics of Hybrid Inverter System
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: As part of research to combine an inverter with a frequency converter, thereby increasing the device frequency limits, the authors investigated the improvement of output waveform distribution of the hybrid system, in an enhanced design to minimize reductions in efficiency due to cascaded connection of the two types of converter. The necessity of system design enabling operation in the oscillation region of the first zero-wave component, but not the second zero-wave component, was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Stability of Co-Based Amorphous Wound Cores Used for Controlling a Switched-Mode Power Supply and Their Optimum Conversion Frequency
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co-based amorphous wound cores for switching-power supply saturable reactors were prepared, and comparing them with permalloy cores, changes in their magnetic properties with time and optimum conversion frequencies were studied. The greatest changes in magnetic properties were recorded for a sample which was not heat-treated. Magnetic field-annealed samples had large initial core losses but were stable over time. Optimum frequency of a high-rectangularity sample was 100 kHz. It was concluded that the high-frequency properties of Co-base amorphous cores are superior to those of permalloy wound cores.

articleTitle: Dynamic Properties of Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Tape Coated with Acicular Ba-Ferrite Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic properties of a particulate film fabricated from acicular Ba-ferrite microparticles, coated onto a plastic tape, were evaluated. Squareness ratio measurements showed that this fine dispersion of particles in paint 1) was clearly oriented in the direction of their easy magnetization axis after orientation in a magnetic field, 2) is much more readily formed into a coating film than hexagonal-plate-form Ba-ferrite particles, and 3) has a smooth magnetic field orientation. The hysteresis measurements showed that acicular Ba-ferrite particles have an excellent perpendicular magnetic anisotropy.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Effect in Magnetic Fluid
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To explore the possibilities of applying films of magnetic fluid in optical devices, birefringence in a magnetic colloid film was studied by measuring the maximum and minimum intensities of transmitted coherent light polarized in directions parallel and perpendicular to an applied magnetic field, the strength of which was varied. From the results, the dependence of phase shifts of orthogonal electric field vector components on the field strength was determined. It is thought that the magnetic particles in the fluid align in chains parallel to the field, thereby inducing the observed differences in transmissivity of light polarized in the parallel and perpendicular directions.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Insoluble Binary System Thin Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Annealing insoluble binary system thin films containing Fe in a magnetic field at temperatures of 200°C or more, causes a sharp increase in coercive force and saturation magnetization. X-ray diffraction of the annealed samples revealed large peaks, which grew larger at increased temperatures, but no such peaks were observed in the control group indicating the rapid formation of Fe clusters. The absence of in-plane anisotropy was verified using X-ray diffraction patterns.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Microstructure of Co-Cr Alloy Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between the magnetocrystalline anisotropy and the microstructure of Co-Cr alloy thin films is discussed. From transmission electron micrographs and X-ray diffraction analysis, it was found that, though no relation exists between the c-axis orientation of the Co-Cr film and a columnar structure, the principal source of the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was the crystal magnetic anisotropy. The Cr segregation and the magnetostrictive effect were also significant contributory factors.

articleTitle: Graphical Circuit Analysis of Orthogonal-Flux Type Transformer
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An original method of graphical analysis is used to investigate the power conversion characteristic of an orthogonal-flux type transformer. Parameters in the analysis include the primary and secondary currents, windings, voltages and powers, the phase angle between a sinusoidal supply voltage and a square wave voltage, and time variations of the primary and secondary magnetic fluxes. Except for discrepancies due to magnetic hysteresis, the analysis results agree well with experimental measurements.

articleTitle: 25-Turn Thin-Film Magnetic Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A small coil pitch is necessary if the number of coil turns is to be increased without lengthening the magnetic yoke and decreasing head efficiency. The performance of a 25-turn thin-film head with a fine coil pitch of 5.5 μm is described, comparing it with a 16-turn, 7 μm pitch head. The head with the finer coil pitch had better current saturation and overwrite characteristics, and the recording density characteristic was nearly the same as for the 16-turn head.

articleTitle: Mechanocardiograph Due to Amorphous Wire-Core Multivibrator Magnetometer
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Application of a noncontact displacement sensor, consisting of a small magnet and amorphous dual-core magnetometer and featuring excellent linearity, to a mechanocardiograph (heart displacement sensor) is described. Detection signals showed linear dependence on magnet displacement (nonlinearity ≪ 1%) for displacements up to 6 mm. The minimum detection resolution was 1 μm, enabling detection of human heart displacement, which ranges from a few to several tens of μm. Cardiac displacement distributions can be obtained, for more complete diagnostics than are possible with electroor magnetocardiographs.

articleTitle: Torque Magnetometer Using A Superconducting Magnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A torque magnetometer developed for use with a 100 kOe superconducting magnet is described. Torques exerted on the sample are transferred to a strain gauge-transducer, the change in resistance detected by a bridge, converted to a digital signal and recorded. This setup allows the bulk of the torque magnetometer mechanism to be located a distance from the sample, thereby facilitating use of a superconducting magnet, with the field parallel to the sample. In this way, even relatively large magnetic anisotropies may be measured.

articleTitle: Magnetics and the New Understanding of Materials Given by the New Frame in Physics
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new framework uniting classical and quantum physics, along with implications for the study of magnetic materials, are discussed. Features of this framework include emphasis on the Schrödinger representation of time-dependent wave functions, which alone enables a continuous transition from classical to quantum mechanical phenomena, and the adoption of an "electron field" model, replacing the vortex ring model of the electron. Consequences for magnetics, such as in statistical thermodynamic treatment of magnetized materials and the manifest nature of the Meisner effect in superconductors, are indicated.

articleTitle: Weather Resistance of CoCr Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Cr content was varied in fabricating samples of CoCr-Permalloy films to investigate magnetic characteristics on the surface and inside the films under two sets of fixed environmental conditions to assess weather resistance. The interior of the films were found to be stable with no change in magnetic properties. On the surface, changes in H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cs</inf> value and in the composition were found. Though samples containing more than 20 at% Cr showed excellent stability.
