articleTitle: Flux Control Method of FOC by Magnetic Fluid
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Methods for controlling the magnetic flux in open type ferrite orthogonal cores (FOCs) by raising, lowering, and inclining them in magnetic fluid, are discussed. It was found that when the open FOC came into contact with the magnetic fluid, increases in both the permeability and the maximum magnetic flux value resulted; that the magnetic flux could be controlled by setting the FOC at an angle to the fluid; and that by arranging the two exciter windings of the open FOC orthogonally and exciting both, the device may be used as a two-dimensional slope sensor.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics of Magneto-Optical Disk with Quadrilayer Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of recording sensitivity and recording conditions on bits recorded on sputtered four-layer GdTbFe film are reported. A correlation was seen between recorded bit length and film optical absorption per unit thickness. As films were made thinner, the resulting bit length grew longer and the film became more sensitive. Fluctuation in bit widths was minimum at a recording power of 5.1 mW and a bias field strength of 500 to 600 Oe. The bit size was determined by the film temperature and coercive force, the bias field, and the temperature gradient in the medium. For 4/5 modulation, the shortest bit length was approximately 1.3 μm.

articleTitle: Effect of Pole-Tip Shape on Recording Characteristics with Thin Film Magnetic Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A number of thin-film magnetic heads with different pole shapes were constructed, and the resulting differences in performance were investigated. The lower poles of prototype heads had protrusions extending toward the medium surface, and positioned differently for different heads. Results indicated that such protrusions act both to reduce negative depressions in reproduced waveforms, and to enable a satisfactory recording density characteristic with less pronounced undulations.

abstract: The contributions of SmCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> and Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l7</inf> (1-5 and 2-17 type) on the magnetization process in ring magnets were investigated. In 8-pole magnetizing, the flux density versus magnetizing voltage characteristics for the two were nearly the same at lower voltages, but as the voltage was raised the 1-5 material characteristic was slightly better. In 60-pole magnetizing, however, as a strong field could not be generated because of the small pole pitch, the larger initial permeability of the 1-5 sample caused its flux density to rise higher at lower voltages than the 2-17 material.

In addition, the magnetic properties of such samples were highly stable, showing no significant deterioration over a period of 30 months.

articleTitle: Read Spacing Loss in Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The read spacing losses in perpendicular magnetic recording have been investigated experimentally for various combinations of heads and media. The spacing loss coefficient K, which is the slope of the line resulting when the spacing loss is plotted against d/λ, has been measured for sinusoidal magnetization. The results show that for a single layer medium, K is almost the same as that in longitudinal recording, and that for a double layer medium, the K value is large at long wavelengths and becomes small with decreasing wavelength. For ring heads in particular, a striking wavelength dependence of K is observed. Such a wavelength dependence results from the change in the distribution and the magnitude of the head sensitivity function with the spacing. Nevertheless, in digital recording the deterioration of recording density characteristics with increasing spacing is small, even at low densities, because of the contribution of harmonics in output signals.

articleTitle: Narrow Track Head Utilizing Electron-Beam Evaporated Fe-Al-Si Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic heads with both laminated and normal Fe-Al-Si cores (the former with SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> between alloy layers) were fabricated, and their properties were evaluated. The permeability of laminated cores was 3.5 times larger than that of nonlaminated cores, which had large eddy current losses. Laminated core heads had larger Q(f) values, and while no significant differences in recording characteristics were observed, the laminated core head had optimum recording currents which were 5-10 mA smaller at each frequency measured. Finally, different permeabilities resulted in different reproduction sensitivities.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Local Magnetic Anisotropy Energy of Amorphous Rare Earth Based Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Studies to determine the local anisotropic energy D of rare earth atoms in amorphous TbFe, TbAg, and DyFe alloys through comparisons of experimental and calculated values for the Arrott plot coefficient at the Curie temperature were studied. Iterative calculations converging on a solution for the magnetization were used in determining the theoretical value of b for different local an isotropy energies D; this method was used to find the D for which the experimental and calculated values of b coincided. Values of D thus obtained ranged from 1.1 to 9.6 (× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> erg/atom).

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Co-Y Amorphous Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In this report, the differences in the magnetic moment, high-field susceptibility and temperature dependence of magnetization between crystalline and amorphous Co-Y alloys are discussed. The amorphous samples have higher magnetic moments than the crystal phase samples. The same tendency was observed in the spin wave dispersion coefficient. Co-40%Y alloy with a Curie temperature of approximately 200 K has no discernable spontaneous volume magnetostriction and no anomaly in the thermal expansion curve.

articleTitle: Bidirectional m/m Transfer Gates for 4 Mb Ion-Implanted Bubble Devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Roles of a compensation conductor on m/m gates for 4 Mb ion-implanted contiguous disk bubble devices were described. The C-loop to S-loop distance was adjusted for gate operation improvement. The compensation conductor cancelled unnecessary magnetic fields near the gate and reduced propagation errors of bubbles near the gate conductor. Bias margins for consecutive transfer operations have been improved even for long data pages.

articleTitle: Asymmetrical Eddy Currents and Concentration Effect of Magnetic Flux in the High Speed Rotating Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Conducting disks rotating at high speed were used to concentrate flux between the poles of an electromagnet, thereby generating a strong local magnetic field. While the disks are in motion between the magnet poles, the eddy currents generated have an asymmetrical distribution, which was calculated by numerical methods. These currents prevent penetration of the disks by the flux, which instead is concentrated in the space between the disks. The measured transmittance at a wavelength of 1.3 μm was 71-73 percent, compared with the theoretical value of 75 percent, throughout most of the YIG ingots, which were 100 mm in length and 8 mm in diameter. The near-infrared Faraday rotation angles in FZ YIG were larger than in YIG grown by the flux method. Finally, the fundamental properties of an isolator designed and fabricated by the authors, and utilizing the FZ YIG, are presented.

articleTitle: Noise Characteristics of Amorphous Rare Earth-Transition Metal Thin Films

articleTitle: Fabrication and Some Magnetic Properties of Amorphous Co-Zr-/(Au,Ag,Pt) Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The addition of Au, Ag, and Pt to Co-Zr alloys was studied as a means of improving soft magnetic properties, particularly at higher Co concentrations. Film samples were formed by RF sputtering, and the saturation magnetostriction, saturation magnetization, and crystallization temperature were measured. Addition of Au resulted in large reductions in magnetostriction, though the soft magnetic properties themselves changed little. Some Ag and Pt compositions also had zero magnetostriction, but the soft magnetic properties when Pt was added were not satisfactory. Data presented dealt primarily with films containing Au.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors studied the effects of the type of substrate rotation speed on Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> films formed by reactive sputtering, varying the layer deposition period D in the range from 2 to 30 Å while holding the film deposition rate R and substrate temperature T constant. Smaller periods D resulted in larger crystal grains. Films formed on glass, alumite, and (111) silicon substrates with small D were highly oriented in the ≪111≫ direction, while alignment in the ≪100≫ direction was enhanced in films deposited on (100) NaCl. Also, highly oriented films tended to exhibit high squareness ratios and low coercivities.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy, Magnetostriction, and Relaxation of Permeability
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic anisotropy (including magnetic anisotropy by magnetic annealing), magnetostriction and relaxation of initial permeability (disaccommodation) of rapidly quenched binary (Fe, Co)-B and other metal-metalloid amorphous alloys, are reviewed. The magnetic anisotropy existing in the as-quenched sample is primarily due to anisotropic stress. A brief description of the origin of the magnetostriction and the induced magnetic anisotropy is also given. The disaccommodation is explained by the inducement of magnetic anisotropy via the free volume in the domain wall. The activation energies evaluated from the disaccommodation for Fe-(B,P) alloys reflect the sizes of the metalloid atoms.

articleTitle: Losses of Grain-Oriented Three Percent Si-Fe with Very High Permeability
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Iron losses in 3 percent Si grain-oriented steel sheets with high magnetic flux densities, prepared by secondary recrystallization, are studied. Low iron losses, as measured in the rolling direction with a 1 kg/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> tension applied, were obtained for several samples. Losses of samples on which glass films were deposited were larger than for laser-irradiated samples, probably due to the contribution of the glass film-iron interface to irreversible magnetization. Observations of magnetic domains in each phase under AC excitation indicated a lower domain density, a higher active magnetic wall number, and more uniform wall movement, than commercial samples.

abstract: Studies to determine the effects of alternating layers of positive-magnetostriction a-CoTi and negative-magnetostriction a-CoNb, to investigate the consequences for the film magnetic properties, and to elucidate the Nb-Ti interdiffusion mechanism, are described. Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf> films, compositionally modulated with wavelengths of 30 to 60 Å, were prepared by sputtering. The CoTi/CoNb coercivity was found to be increased compared with CoNb, CoTi, and CoNbTi films. The compositionally modulated structure changes to a simple periodic structure through low-temperature heat treatment, but this transition is apparently reversible at higher temperatures through some anomalous diffusion mechanism.

articleTitle: Potential Well Vertical Bloch Line Propagation by Bias Pulse
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors used simulations to study the possibility of employing ribbons of high-coercivity film, separated by an isolation layer from magnetic bubble material, to generate magnetostatic potential wells facilitating the stable propagation of vertical Bloch line (VBL) pairs. The stray field generated by surface charge at domain walls was taken into account in determining the isolation layer thickness and coercivity of the high-coercivity film, resulting in a potential well amplitude enabling stable propagation. Simulations indicated that stable propagation is indeed possible by this method.

articleTitle: Designs and Characteristics of 2 μm Period Ion-Implanted Propagation Tracks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of the shape of ion-implanted (into YSmLuCaGeIG) propagation tracks on the operating margin in bubble memory devices were studied. A snake pattern was used, with a period of 2 μm and pattern width of 0.7 μm, varying the cusp angle θ (i.e., the cusp depth). The cusp angle dependencies of bias margin width (50 Oe drive) and minimum drive field indicated that for a single loop, the smaller the cusp angle, the better the margin. However consequent reduction of the distance between adjacent cells led to jumping errors, and the optimum margin occurred for θ = 90°. A minimum drive field of 58 Oe and bias margin width of 48 Oe (70 Oe drive) were obtained.

articleTitle: Simulation of Vertical Bloch Line Propagation Under the Potential Well by Conductor Current
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Computer simulations were conducted to study propagation of vertical Bloch lines under the influence of a sinusoidal magnetic potential generated by a conductor current. The simulation was performed for 11 stripe domains, with domain walls of infinite length carrying periodic data trains, in typical magnetic bubble material; as the driving field, a trapezoidal pulse field was applied. It was found that for a conductor current of 1 mA and a bias field of from 30 to 40 Oe, a sufficient propagation margin of around 7 Oe may be obtained.

articleTitle: Amorphous Magnetism Microscopic and Macroscopic Magnetic Anisotropies
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Characteristic features of amorphous magnetism are described. Recent progress in a theory of the electronic states in amorphous Fe alloys is reviewed. Both microscopic and macroscopic magnetic anisotropies in amorphous alloys are discussed. The application of magnetic methods to the study of nonequilibrium systems would be effective.

articleTitle: Measurement of Magnetoelastic Effect for Isotropic Thick Alloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: While there are numerous reports on the magnetoelastic (magnetostrictive) effect in uniaxially anisotropic soft magnetic films, no such studies have been reported for isotropic films. A strain gauge and B-H meter were used to determine the anisotropy fields ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> induced by uniaxial strain e in an isotropic Fe-Si-Al film, and from this found the strain sensitivity η. The value of η thus determined was far smaller than the strain sensitivity for the bulk material. The discrepancy may be explained by the application of a model for anisotropic samples to isotropic films, or to a small reverse magnetostriction effect.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetostatic coupling between layers in multilayer films enables more complex domain structures than are possible in single-layer films. Both high-speed sputtering and vacuum deposition were used to form films in which magnetic (Fe, Ni) and nonmagnetic (Si, SiO, C) layers alternate. Due to interdiffusion at layer boundaries, sputtered Fe-Si multilayer films metamorphosed into films of alternating layers of ferromagnetic Fe-rich Fe-Si and nonmagnetic Si-rich Si-Fe, which layers are magnetostatically coupled.

articleTitle: Read-After-Write Characteristics of Ring-Type Heads for Perpendicular CoCr Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Research into the recording density and recording current characteristics of perpendicular CoCr media is reported. CoCr alloy films were either directly formed on a polyimide substrate or on intermediate layers of Ge, Si and Ti, 0.03 μm thick. The recording reproduction properties where measured from the contact conditions of the head and media at relative speed of 2.5 m/s. It was found that it is possible to obtain high-density perpendicular recording reproduction, using a ring-type head composed of high-saturation magnetic flux density material near the optical gap together with CoCr media formed on a Ge base.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The increase in perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in RF sputtered Gd-Co films with application of a negative bias voltage is thought to originate in structural changes due to resputtering effects. Dual-ion-beam sputtering was used to form Gd-Co films, and the relation between perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and resputtering was studied. In experiments using both dual-ion-beam sputtering and a single ion gun, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> decreased monotonically with increasing Gd concentration. articleTitle: Evaporated Fe-Ni Films for a Back Layer of Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media I: the Origin of High Coercivity

abstract: The cause of the high coercive force of permalloy evaporated films was investigated. The ultimate origin of the high coercive force in permalloy evaporated films was found to be magnetic elastic anisotropy causing perpendicular anisotropy. The perpendicular anisotropy generates stripe domains which make magnetic inversion very difficult, producing a high coercive force.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of Bloch Line and Bloch Wall Dynamics by Lumped-Constant Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A lumped constant model, treating forces acting on vertical Bloch lines as a lumped force, was used in a two-dimensional simulation of the motion of Bloch lines and Bloch walls. Relations for forces acting tangentially and normally to the wall were derived, and the mobilities of VBL and Bloch walls for single VBL and for VBL pairs were obtained as functions of the time increment Δt used, with the distance LL between grid points as a parameter. The accuracy of the simulation results as compared with theory was within 1 to 2 percent, depending on both LL and Δt. This method thus enables fairly accurate simulation by microcomputer of VBL and Bloch wall dynamics in a short time.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method was proposed for introducing hyperthermia to destroy or halt the growth of tumors by means of electro-magnetic induction, generating an eddy current which raises the temperature locally. Using a two-dimensional model, it was found that appropriate application of a uniform ac magnetic field, together with two local magnetic fields, enabled the formation of high eddy current densities (hot spots) in two-dimensional conductors. The same method may, in principle, be applied to three-dimensional conductors.

publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Dust cores were originally developed for use in carrier telecommunication inductors, but have been replaced by ferrite cores. At the same timie, high frequency switching is widely used in the regulators of compact electrical equipment. Duist cores have two main features: unsaturated magnetic flux densities under external magnetic fields, and low power losses. As a result they are widely used in regulators. Here, the revival of applications of dust cores to regulators are summarized.

articleTitle: Effect of Resputtering on Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy in Amorphous GdCo Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to control resputtering during the sputtering formation of amorphous thin films, a wire mesh in DC sputtering equipment were used to suppress resputtering, and the effects of resputtering on magnetic anisotropy in GdCo films were studied. The measured values for Keff and M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> indicated that nearly all films had in-plane magnetizations, and under the film deposition conditions, through which resputtering did not occur, a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was not induced. Possible reasons for this include a low deposition rate (~15 Å/min) and small film thicknesses (650 Å).

articleTitle: Structure and Annealing Effect of Co-CoO Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Film formed on a slide glass was annealed in a vacuum for five hours to investigate the effects of annealing on magnetic properties and film structure. The density of the Co high-density section near the film surface was found to be almost equal to that of the film fabricated in pure Ar gas, and this seems to be the origin of the observed increase in M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and the decrease in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> (⊥) and K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>. Compared with measurements before annealing, the rising edges found from channel numbers 200 and 320 after annealiing are very steep, showing that separation between the Co and CoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> layers had progressed.

articleTitle: Multipolar Parametric Induction Motor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Four- and six-pole parametric motors were tested to investigate uses as low speed multipolar motors generating high torques. The four-pole parametric motor adopted toroidally wound Fe-Si plates in exciting magnetic circuits, and operated without a load at 1450 rpm. Though the output P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> and efficiency η were small, they should be greatly improved with better motor designs. A six-pole motor, built on the same principles, was successfully operated at an unloaded speed of 850 rpm, for a synchronized speed of 1000 rpm.

articleTitle: Improvement of Performance of the Magnetic Frequency Tripler
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Numerical analysis was used to obtain the characteristics resulting from connection of a filter to the input of magnetic frequency triplers, which utilize the nonlinear characteristics of magnetic cores to obtain triple-frequency outputs. The magnetization characteristic of the circuit saturation reactor was approximated by two connected straight lines; voltage and load characteristics were found using mode and vector analyses. The input voltage characteristics, load characteristics, and input current waveforms for assumed circuit parameters are presented.

articleTitle: Lumped Constant and Distributed Models of Vertical Bloch Lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The lumped constant model for vertical Bloch lines (in which a VBL is treated as a single point in the domain wall) is modified to take into account repulsive forces between VBLs and other factors, thereby making it as accurate as the conventional distributed VBL model. Simulations were performed based on the two models, for translational motion of a circular bubble with two VBL in the domain wall; the q value dependence of the skew angle, which does not appear in results for simple lumped constant models, is found in the results for the modified lumped constant model.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics of BaM Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Evaluations of recording density using ring heads with relatively wide apertures on thin films of different Δθ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> used for disk media (2 inch ø), and evaluations of the thermal stability of BaM thin films are reported. The possibility of obtaining a high recording density thin film with small Δθ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> was clearly established. Changes in residual magnetization with respect to temperature variation were measured, revealing that when the film was left to stand for 15 h at 250°C approximately 10 percent thermal demagnetization occurred, and the film was almost completely demagnetized at 375°C.

articleTitle: Parallel Stream Type HGMS Filter Performance for Recovery of Ferromagnetic Particles
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of the filtering element in a parallel stream type HGMS filter on the filter performance over time was investigated. A filtering element was constructed by spacing ferromagnetic wires (of radius 50 μm) at different spacings and with different spacer thicknesses. The accumulation of magnetite suspended in water in the filter was photographed. Results indicated that a spacer thickness of 0.3 mm, and wire spacing of 0.5 mm, yielded the best performance, and that a magnetic field of 3 kOe was sufficient in actual operation.

articleTitle: Film Thickness Effect on Magnetic Properties of Electroless Co Alloy Films for Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes work on fabricating a film with a specific dependency on certain transverse magnetic properties by controlling the density of the complexing agent in the electroless plating bath. It was found that the dependence of magnetic properties on the film thickness and the orientation at inital deposition can be regulated by controlling the bath compositions. The conclusion is that this kind of change in magnetic properties caused by inequality with respect to the film thickness direction in the microstructure must be taken into consideration when designing media.

articleTitle: A Study of Amorphous Alloy Cutting Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The large magnetostriction of iron-base amorphous alloys causes deterioration in magnetic properties during annealing, cutting, and other high-stress processing. The authors formed elliptical wound iron cores using Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">79</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> film, annealed them in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas at 450°C, and impregnated them in epoxy and silicon resins before hardening under various conditions. Measurements of the high-frequency iron loss and AC B-H characteristics indicated an increase in coercive force after impregnation, and a doubling of the iron loss between impregnation and cutting. The original iron loss could be restored by polishing.

articleTitle: Effect of Dimensions on Power Losses in Mn-Zn Ferrite Cores
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Two types of Mn-Zn ferrite cores-high-permeability samples with low hysteresis losses, and converter materials with good high-frequency characteristics but large hysteresis losses-were immersed in acid to gradually reduce their external dimensions, and the resulting change in large-amplitude losses and small-signal characteristics was measured. The core loss per cycle was lowered with reduction in dimensions for the high-permeability samples, but not for the converter materials; and the hysteresis loss increased for very small high-permeability core sizes, while that of the converter materials remained constant. These differences are explained in terms of the different microstructures and domain structures in the materials.

articleTitle: Effects of Atomic Replacement on Magnetism in Nd2Fe14B
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors report the changes in properties of tetragonal Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B, the main phase present in Nd-Fe-B permanent magnets, as various elements (Co, Ni, Cu, V, Al, Cr, Mn) were substituted for Fe. Substitutions did not change the tetragonal crystal structure. Results of Curie temperature measurements could not be explained solely in terms of changes in Fe-Fe interatomic distances. Except for Co, all substitutions resulted in decreases in the magnetization at room temperature.

articleTitle: Erasing Characteristics of Magneto-Optical Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Erasing characteristics of magneto-optical media (thick TbFe film formed by triode RF sputtering on grooved plastic, with an SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> protective layer) are reported. Three disks, with varying Tb concentrations, coercivities and other properties, were used in experiments. Conditions for erasing prerecorded signals were determined for each of these disks; erasing was possible at the same power as writing (4 mW) for two of the disks. It was concluded that disks with a large coercive force yield more favorable erasing characteristics, while composition is not directly related.

articleTitle: Materials of Orthogonal Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relations between the properties of materials used in orthogonal cores and the core performance were studied. The magnetic flux control, ambient temperature, core temperature increase and waveform distortion characteristics are presented for an amorphous orthogonal core (AOC) and an Mn-Zn ferrite orthogonal core (FOC). It is concluaded that the orthogonal magnetic flux in orthogonal cores made of layered amorphous or metal film acts to greatly increase the relucetance, so that the original properties of the material used in the core do not appear, the permeability of the laminated core becomes smaller, and magnetization characteristics are linear.

articleTitle: A Magneto-Optical Disk Testing System
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A device for automatic measurement of bit error rates and identification of the position of errors in magneto-optical disks was constructed, and used in actual disk evaluations. The microcomputer-controlled device enables measurements on either individual tracks or on groups of tracks, and outputs bit error rates and error distributions. In actual tests, the bit error rate of grooved TbFeCo magneto-optical disks was found to be on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>.

articleTitle: Magnetization Distribution Analysis for Thin Film Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Taking into consideration the effect of leakage flux from the medium, an analysis of the curling state in the demagnetizing field was employed to study head film magnetizattion processes during readout of magnetically recorded signals. The analysis yielded values for the magnetostatic, anisotropy and Zeeman energies, as well as the angle of inclination θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> of the magnetic moment at the head tip surface and the region D over which the moment deviates from the easy axis direction. From these results the magnetization distribution was calculated. The Kerr effect was used to measure actual magnetization distributions, and good agreement was obtained between theory and experiment.

articleTitle: Thermoplastic Magnet Having Highly Improved Heat-Resistance
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Plastic magnets were formed with SmCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> powder using nylon-12 (PA-12), and PBT (conventional type and low-viscosity type) binders. The magnetic properties and resistance to thermal degradation were studied. Whereas general magnetic properties were best for PA-12 magnets, such properties as the flexure strength and heat resistance were better for PBT magnets, directly reflecting the binder properties. When metal, oxide, a heat-resistant coupling agent, and a conventional coupling agent were used to coat SmCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> powder, the best stability against heating was obtained for the metal coating (stable to above 300°C), followed by the oxide coating, heat-resistant coupling agent, and conventional coupling agent.

articleTitle: Operating Characteristics of a Trial Audio-Frequency-Range Magnetic Amplifier System Using Amorphous Magnetic Cores
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The application of a cobalt-base amorphous magnetic core in an "all-magnetic" audio amlifier is reported. A two-stage Lufcy circuit was driven by a 100 kHz power supply. The control characteristics showed good linearity, and amplification by 56 dB was achieved. The frequency characteristic for sine wave input signals was nearly flat over the entire audible frequency range, and overall sound quality was good.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy of Tb-Co Amorphous Films Sputtered In H2-Added Ar Gas
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Tb-Co amorphous films are prime candidates for use as magneto-optical recording media, but the method commonly employed to induce a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, bias sputtering, is not compatible with glass substrates. In this case RF sputtering is used in an H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Ar gas mixture, without a substrate bias voltage, to form Tb-Co films. As the hydrogen partial pressure P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H2</inf> was increased, the film saturation magnetization M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> decreased, the uniaxial anisotropy constant K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> increased, and the Kerr hysteresis loop became more rectangular. For P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H2</inf> = 10 percent, samples had an extremely large positive anisotropy even when the Tb content was varied over a wide range.

abstract: To better understand the magnetic structures of magnetically anisotropic GdCo and GdFe amorphous films, Hall characteristics were measured under strong pulsed magnetic fields up to 40 T. Anomalous magnetization loops were observed for GdCo and Bi-doped GdFe film, differing from data obtained for weaker fields, and changes in residual Hall voltage with the in-plane magnetic field were also determined.

articleTitle: Microstructure and Corrosion Resistance of CoCr Thin Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The microstructure of CoCr films varies with the fabrication conditions. The surface structure deteriorates faster when Cr density is low. When the grain structure is very fine, the deterioration is faster when the grain interfaces are very clearly-defined. No significant difference was found in Ms decrease when an SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> protective film was deposited on the CrCo. The thickness was varied to 100 Å, 300 Å or 500 Å. A protective film thickness of at most 100 Å proved to be effective in producing good corrosion resistance.

articleTitle: Stability Test of GdTbFe at High Temperatures
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The reliability of rare earth-transition metal (RE-TM) alloy films with a multilayer structure, which attain a high signal-to-noise ratio, is discussed. In order to study the stability of multilayer magneto-optic (M-O) media which consist of a GdTbFe layer sandwiched between nitride layers, heating tests (380-480°C) have been conducted. Magneto-optic properties were evaluated using Kerr hysteresis loops. In a high-temperature environment (400°C), the coercive force (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) is found to increase, while the Curie temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) decreases. It seems that these changes in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c result from a decrease in effective RE content. However, samples using SUS-304 as a reflector exhibit less change in Hc than those using Al at 400°C, and samples heated in vacuum (2×10<sup>-6</sup> Torr) exhibit a small change in H<sub>c</sub>. From these results, it is felt that such phenomena in high temperature environments are caused by selective oxidation of RE atoms. There is little change in the magneto-optic properties at 380°C. Therefore, multilayer M-O media using AlN offer promise as high-stability materials for use in thermomagnetic recording.</sub>

articleTitle: A Problem Concerning the Mesh Partition in Magnetization Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of mesh partitioning on results obtained in numerical analysis of magnetization distribution using the two-dimensional integration method are discussed, and the results of this method compared with those obtained by the finite element method. Square and round magnetic bodies were treated as single magnetic domains in linear calculations, and were partitioned into square and triangular meshes with an aspect ratio h/w of from 1.0 to 2.1. It was found that to obtain a close approximation to the actual magnetization, a square mesh with an aspect ratio of about one must be used.

articleTitle: Reciprocal Action of Multilayered Permalloy Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A magnetoresistive (MR) sensor consisting of two pairs of multilayered (FeNi layers sandwiched between SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) MR elements was constructed, and the effects of the signal magnetic tilt angle, temperature, and input power on the sensor output were studied. Constant current driving was employed, taking advantage of a mutual bias effect, to obtain an output with small temperature dependence. The exact relation of output to input depended on the nature of the signal magnetic field.

articleTitle: Magnetism and Structure of Compositionally Modulated Fe-Gd Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Electron-beam heating was used to evaporate Fe and Gd on glass in attempts to form compositionally modulated thin films with vertical periodicity. The film structure was varied, from 300 6-Å layers to 25 250-Å layers. Small-angle X-ray diffraction confirmed the formation of compositionally modulated cycles greater than 20 Å; for smaller periodicities, the structure was amorphous. A compensation temperature of 200 K was taken to indicate that magnetic moments within Fe and Gd layers were ferromagnetic but oppositely directed.

articleTitle: Preparation of TbFeCo Films by Two Source Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic and magneto-optical properties of TbFeCo films formed on glass substrates by two-source (FeCo and Tb) magnetron sputtering, while varying the RF input power, Ar gas pressure, and subtrate rotation speed, are reported. By independent variation of the input power for the two sources, many different film compositions were obtained. The film M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, perpendicular anisotropic energy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub> and Kerr rotation angle ⊥<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> were all fairly stable for substrate rotation speeds of 20 rpm or above, below this all three values increased as the speed was decreased.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Magnetic Perpendicular Anisotropy of Vapor Quenched Fe Films Using Mössbauer Effect
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Pure Fe films were produced by rf sputtering under several Ar gas pressures and were investigated with an SEM and Mössbauer effect. In the Mössbauer spectra, a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was observed for films made under high Ar gas pressures, while an in-plane anisotropy was seen for films made under low Ar gas pressures. The anisotropy of the films did not change after one hour of annealing at 300 K. Films made under low Ar gas pressures have a fine fiber structure, while films made under high Ar gas pressures have a columnar structure separated by distinct boundaries. Assuming that the magnetic interaction within the columnar structure is weak, the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy of the films under high Ar gas pressures can be explained by the shape anisotropy of the columnar structure.

articleTitle: A Bubble Generation Mechanism for Ion-Implanted Bubble Devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new mechanism of bubble generation in ion-implanted bubble devices has been proposed based on minimum generation current characteristies. This model shows that bubble nucleation requires a 180° magnetic wall shift in the transition layer between the ion-implanted and bubble layers which can be used to logically explain bubble generation in ion-implanted devices.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of 6.5 wt% Si-Fe Alloy Single Crystal with Phase Separation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic properties of 6.5 wt% Si-Fe alloy, annealed at 1100°C, oil-quenched, then annealed at 630°C for different durations and again oil-quenched, and consisting of a mixed B2 + DO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> phase, are reported. Dark-field images showed DO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ordered structures as fine particles in samples annealed at 630°C for 3 hours, but the volume of the particles increased and became lamellar in the (100) direction, for longer annealing times. Changes in the soft magnetic properties, permeability, and coercive force were also measured.

articleTitle: Optimum Design Method for Magnetizers and its Application
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Improvements in magnetizers that enable generation of a specified surface flux distribution in apparatus incorporating permanent magnets are described. The finite element method is used to design the shape of the magnetizer by tracing backward along the magnetization curve of the magnet. This process is outlined for a ferrite-based plastic magnet; the shape obtained was confirmed to yield the desired flux distribution.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Domain Observations for CoZr/NiFe Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties and domain structures of amorphous Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">90</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>/ polycrystalline Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">81</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> (wt%) multilayer films, candidates for use as the pole pieces of thin-film heads, were investigated. After sputter-forming film samples in a 400 Oe magnetic field, they were annealed with a 480 Oe field either in the easy axis and then the hard axis directions, or rotating relative to the sample. The latter type of annealing resulted in increased permeability and a weakened anisotropy field. Observations of domain structures indicated that the multilayer films have stable and reproducible domains in both magnetized and demagnetized states.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Y-Fe-B system Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The results of studies on the relation between the microstructure and magnetic properties of Y-Fe-B system alloys which were first quenched and then annealed are reported. A coercive force of 6 kOe and saturation magnetic moment of 61 emu/g were obtained for an Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub> sample with annealing at 700°C for one hour. Aging at 660°C brought about increases in both coercivity and saturation magnetic moment up to one hour, after which these deteriorated; X-ray diffraction studies indicated the presence of an unknown α phase, which grew with the aging time and was inferred to be the cause of the deterioration.

articleTitle: Single-Edge Sensitive Single-Pole Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To suppress dips in recording density characteristics during reproduction of perpendicular recorded signals, the possibility of a read head with high sensitivity at the waveform trailing edge, and low sensitivity at the leading edge (single-edge sensitive) was studied. Through enlarged model experiments, the possibility of such a head was verified; an increased output may be expected by making the field edges sharper.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of the Rapidly Quenched Sm2 (Co1-xMx)17 (M=Fe,Mn) Alloy Ribbons
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to investigate the hard magnetic properties of rapidly quenched Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>-type multi-element alloy ribbons, Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.5) and Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> (0 ≤ X &3x02264; 0.25) alloy ribbons were fabricated under various conditions and the effects of the third element on the hard magnetic properties and structure were examined. A remarkable increase in the value of <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> was found at high roll velocities (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub>). The maximum value of <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> was found to be about 7 kOe for Sm-Co-Mn alloy ribbons and about 2 kOe for Sm-Co-Fe alloy ribbons. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that an ordered Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> phase was formed at low V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub>, while a single disordered Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> phase (TbCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>-type) was formed at high V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub>.

articleTitle: Properties of Carbon Protective Films for Magnetic Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Carbon (graphite) film, which has a lubricating effect, was studied as a replacement for SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film in protecting magnetic disks. Carbon films were formed by ion-beam sputtering, with stable amorphous films obtained regardless of the sputtering conditions. Carbon films had high scratch hardness and good thermal conductivity, as well as a higher wear resistance than SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. For sufficiently thin films, friction coefficients were small, enabling use as protective film for magnetic disks.

articleTitle: Reproduce Characteristics of YMRH
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The reproduction characteristics of trial-fabricated yoke-type MR heads (YAMRHs) are reported. It was found that most of the tape rubbing noise for I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> ≤ 10 mA was accounted for by tape erasure noise, while for I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> ≫ 10 mA low-frequency components of the thermal noise gradually become dominant over erasure noise. However, Barkhausen noise was found to be dominant over both, and must be suppressed if deterioration of eye patterns is to be avoided.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Metastable Fe-Al Alloys Produced by Vapor Quenching
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe-Al alloys were prepared by the standard RF sputtering method (vapor quenching), their compositions were determined by EPMA, X-ray diffraction and Mössbauer effect analyses were performed, and film magnetic properties were measured. Sputtered alloys were in a nearly complete state of disorder. At higher Al concentrations, an amorphous phase appeared, and marked deviation from the simple dilution law governing the composition dependence of the magnetization was observed. The Mössbauer spectra of sputtered bcc films suggested the existence of a magnetic perpendicular anisotropy.

articleTitle: Design Considerations of Permalloy Propagation Patterns for Hybrid Bubble Devices with a 2 μm Period
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Bubble propagation margins along permalloy patterns on various spacer thicknesses for two types of propagation patterns, the so called half disc and wide gap patterns, were studied, and two error modes were observed. One of these was a gap error or a failure of the bubble to cross the gap, and the other was shoulder error. These errors are both caused by the spacer thickness which affects the bias magnetic field. To overcome these errors, a new pattern shape was introduced that has characteristics which are nearly independent of the spacer thickness.

articleTitle: Block Replicate Gates for Ion-Implanted Bubble Devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A two-layer conductor is used for replicating bubbles in ion-implanted bubble devices. The first layer is a parallel conductor used to cut the bubbles which have been stretched by the hairpin conductor in the second layer. There was sufficient operation margin even with a low drive field and a bias field margin of 22.5 Oe was obtained at a drive field of 60 Oe. Error brought on by the stretch pulse will be improved by lengthening the corner pattern. In addition, replicate-in/transfer-out operation was verified.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optics: Its Past and Present
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A very brief survey is made of the research conducted on magneto-optics in recent years. A highly Bi-substituted rare earth iron garnet is described as a candidate magneto-optical material. PtMnSb, representing a new type of metallic magneto-optical material, is grown in thin film form for use in magneto-optical recording media. Semi-magnetic semiconductors such as CdMnTe are also new candidates for uses in other areas. Applications as magneto-optical device elements in various areas of optoelectronics also show great promise.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties for Fe3Al Single Crystal of the Two Regions with α + B2 and α + DO3 Structures
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Al alloys with a relatively stable dual-phase range α + B2 and α + DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) were produced and the magnetic properties studied, to determine the effect of α phases on Sendust soft magnetic properties. The crystal magnetic anisotropy constant K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> was found to change for different phase combinations; its absolute value was smaller for alloys with α + DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> than for α + B2. Electron micrographs showed maze-like structures of scale 1 μm or less in the dual-phase material. Further studies of the effect of such dual-phase structures on magnetic properties are underway.

articleTitle: The Magnetic Inhomogeneous Structure of Fe65Ni35 Alloy by Means of Polarized Neutron Small-Angle Scattering

abstract: To test a model for the magnetically inhomogeneous structure in Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">65</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">35</inf> invar alloys, according to which paramagnetic clusters are formed in Fe-rich regions, a polarized neutron scattering device was used to measure the polarized neutron small-angle scattering in natural (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">65</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nat</sup>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">35</inf>) and isotopic (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">65</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">62</sup>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">35</inf>) samples. Measured deviations from average scattering amplitude densities coincided with values predicted on the basis of the model, and provided information on the shapes of the paramagnetic clusters.

articleTitle: Hard Magnetic Properties of Rapidly Quenched Sm-Co Alloys with Al, Si and B Elements (I) Structural Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: We carefully investigated the roll circumferential velocity dependence and Sm concentration dependence of the magnetic characteristics of Sm-Co-based alloy ribbons (with their various Sm concentrations) made by the single-roll method. The results showed that the magnetic characteristics of these ribbons are strongly controlled by the orientation of the grains and the grain diameters in the high temperature region (which are frozen in during the rapid quenching treatment). This time we concentrated on the grain growth process of the ribbons, and by rapidly quenching threeelement alloys (adding Al, Si, or B), we tried varying the growth conditions. We studied the amount of change in grain growth and orientation with each of these elements. We also studied the correlation between the metal composition and the magnetic characteristics and clarified the effects of the changing conditions on the characteristics.

articleTitle: Application of Co-Zr Based Amorphous Thin Film to Perpendicular Recording Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Since during the manufacture of thin film heads, the properties of Co-base amorphous films tend to deteriorate, the authors investigated the effects of head production processes on such films. Films were RF sputtered and annealed in a rotating magnetic field, and used to construct perpendicular heads, with film properties measured before and after head construction. Deterioration of μ and M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> with machining was due in part to the large magnetostriction coefficient, and to heating and pressure application during machining.

articleTitle: Ferromagnetic Resonance of Amorphous Ribbons Fe78B13Si9
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Changes in the ferromagnetic resonance field in amorphous Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">78</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sub> ribbons with surface polishing and annealing are reported. Grooves 5 μm or so deep in the surface tend to greatly affect the magnetic anisotropy, hence samples were polished with emery paper and by electrolysis and the FMR strength and anisotropy field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> determined after each polishing. Such polishing led to a general decrease in the resonant field and in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>. Annealing of polished samples at 400° in nitrogen was found to further reduce the FMR field, but had no effect on H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>.

articleTitle: Structures and Dynamic Characteristics of Magneto-Optical Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Changes with time are reported in the reflection factor, magneto-optical rotation angle, coercive force, C/N, and error rate of magneto-optical disks with four different structures (A-D) on PMMA substrates, at 45°C and 55°C and humidities of 90 and 60 percent. Disks of structure A, without a protective film between substrate and medium, showed rapid deterioration of properties; structures C and D tended to develop cracks, making measurements impossible. Structure B disks were estimated to have a service lifetime of 4 to 6 years at 25°C and 50% RH; for longer lifetimes, PC or glass substrates are desired.

articleTitle: Video Head Multi-Layer Amorphous Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The electromagnetic conversion and other characteristics of heads fabricated using Co-Zr-Nb multilayer amorphous alloy films are reported. Heads were used in a VHS type VTR to measure the recording/reproduction characteristics, which, using metal tape (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 1300 Oe), showed an output higher by 2 to 4 dB at 5 MHz than other head materials. Outputs were 0.25 mV (normal tape) and 0.44 mV (metal tape) at 5 MHz, for a track width of 24 μ and a gap length of 0.69 μ, sufficient to enable use as a head for metal media.

articleTitle: Magnetic Image Effect in Superconducting Magnet and Magnetization Measurement
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic image effect (flux distortion due to the Meissner effect) in superconducting magnets (SCM's) was studied both theoretically and experimentally. Changes with temperature in the magnetic moment of a current loop coil (as measured by a VSM) were observed; sudden drops at 15 K and 7 K corresponded to the superconducting temperatures of Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn and NbTi used in the SCM. Experimental results for both image effects and residual magnetic fields agreed with calculations by the finite element method. The image effect tends to cause overestimation of susceptibility and underestimation of the magnetization.

articleTitle: Magnetic Characteristics of Initial Deposition Layer of CoCr Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: New information is presented on the initial deposition layer of CoCr film which is divided into three regions. In the first region, up to 300 Å from the substrate, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub> and M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> are small, crystallization is disturbed and there is no perpendicular anisotropy. From 300 Å to 0.1 μm, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub> and M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> are very large, suggesting that this layer is formed of segregated Cr fine grains. Above 0.1, μm the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub> curve gently slopes down as the film thickness increases, M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> is constant, and the crystal orientation is good. Thus, it was confirmed that there is an intermediate level within the initial formation layer of CoCr films which has very large H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub> and M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> values.

articleTitle: Crystalographic Orientation of Continuously Sputtered Co-Cr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The dependence of film crystal orientation on film thickness for several Co-Cr films formed by dc planar magnetron sputtering with a variety of deposition mask arrangements was investigated. Special attention was paid to the initial layer. The dependence of magnetic properties on film thickness was found to be strongly influenced by the mask arrangement, especially by the distance between the mask edge and the roll, and by the initial incidence angle for the sputtered atoms. It was found that controlling these parameters properly is extremely important in continuous sputtering.

articleTitle: Transformation Points in High Permeability Alloy "Super Sendust"
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetization in "Super Sendust" alloys (1-4% Ni, 4-8% Si, 2-6% Al, balance Fe) depends to a great extent on composition and conditions of heat treatment. The alloy hardness, electrical resistivity, saturation magnetization, and crystal structure as functions of temperature and heat treatment were studied. Setting Si and Al contents at 6 and 4 percent and substituting 0-7% Ni for Fe, various material properties went through extreme at 3.2% Ni. Structural analyses revealed a shift from body-centered to face-centered cubic when the temperature was raised to 710°C. These and other abnormal changes in alloy properties are thought to be closely related to a DO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-type superlattice structure.

articleTitle: Anisotropy Field Change by Annealing in He+/Ne+ Ion-Implanted Bubble Garnet Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Bubble garnet films, (YSmLuGd)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (FeGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>, were implanted with He, N, and Ne ions at 100-200 keV and annealed at 350 to 600°C, and changes in the maximum lattice strain, (Δa/a)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>, and in the effective anisotropy field, Δ(H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>-4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>), were measured by double-crystal X-ray diffraction and ferromagnetic resonance. Lattice strain in layers implanted with He, N, and Ne ions decreased monotonically with annealing. The change in anisotropy field initially increases with heat treatment for samples implanted with heavy ion doses, then decreases. This increase was attributed to changes in the saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and magnetostriction coefficient λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub>.

articleTitle: Magnetic Domains in Single-Pole Magnetic film Heads and Recording Characteristics
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Domain structures in the main pole films of single-pole heads were studied, including microscopic domain observations and measurements of domain inclination angles θ (between the easy axis direction and the track width direction), and the effects of domain structures on recording using Co-Cr media investigated. Although isolated readback voltages were larger for large angles θ, other characteristics, noise in particular, were better for smaller θ. It was concluded that small inclination angles θ are necessary for high density, high fidelity recording.

articleTitle: Fundamental Magnetoelastic Waves in a Conductive Thin Magnetostrictive Slab
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Large changes in the velocity of magnetoelastic waves (MEWs) with a small bias field can be realized only in media with a high magnetostriction and high permeability, such as certain Fe-based amorphous materials. However, as the latter are highly conductive, a new theoretical analysis of MEW propagation in a thin magneto-strictive conductor, which takes micro-eddy current losses into account, is presented. A matrix formulation together with appropriate boundary conditions yields the MEW dispersion relation, which is solved by numerical calculations. Results indicate that controllable changes in MEW velocity are accompanied by propagation losses.

articleTitle: Dynamic Characteristics of TbFeCo Magneto-Optical Disk with CLV Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A device for magneto-optical disk evaluation, employing a constant linear velocity (CLV) disk rotating system and small lightweight optical head, is described. The evaluator can be used to record and reproduce signals in a CD format, and to measure frame error rates. Relations between the linear velocity and the frame error rate, and between the error rate and the minimum bit length, were determined for TbFeCo-PMMA disks. Results indicated that error rates deteriorated rapidly for minimum bit lengths below 1.5 μm, in agreement with observed changes in eye patterns.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Recording Characteristics Of Ring Head and Co-Cr/Co-Zr-Mo Double-Layer Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A Winchester-type Mn-Zn ferrite ring head (gap length 0.3 μm) was used to evaluate the perpendicular recording/reproduction characteristics of Co-Cr/Co-Zr-Mo double-layer and Co-Cr single-layer media. The absolute reproduced output voltage was higher at high medium H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> values for the double-layer film, but there was no great difference in the D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> versus H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> characteristics of the two. Noise spikes were observed when reproducing from double-layer films after DC erasure, and was attributed to the underlayer. Except for this noise, the double-layer media exhibited more favorable characteristics.

abstract: The magnetization process in Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Fe was studied in relation to the concentration of Ni and the degree of order S, to clarify the role of the antiphase boundary during domain wall displacement. articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Layer Structure Compound La (CrxMn1-x)2Ge2

abstract: The La(Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> system (with a Mn-Ge-La-Ge-Mn layer structure) was studied in order to clarify the effect of the manganese 3d electrons, and to find properties with potential applications. articleTitle: δ-Dependence of Magnetism in the C15 Laves Phase System HfCo2+δ
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Investigations of the magnetic properties of non-stoichiometric HfCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>+δ led to the discovery of ferromagnetism for δ ≫ 0.8. Homogeneous samples formed by plasma jet-melting in argon were annealed to obtain single phase crystals, and then quenched. X-ray diffraction confirmed the existence of a single-phase with C15 type structure for -0.2 ≪ δ ≪ 1.2, but a single phase could not be obtained at other compositions. The range of ferromagnetic behavior, susceptibility, and other magnetic properties are described.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of Stripe Domain Stretching
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Computer simulations of stripe domain stretching processes were performed for several domains together, taking into account the effects of conductors and grooves. For a 2 μm thick garnet film supporting 5 μm bubbles and a conductor current of 10 mA, the effects of conductor and groove fields on domains near the center is constant for about 11 or more stripe domains. Simulations showed that stripe domains may be stretched even when several exist together, and that stretching under various bias conditions is possible by appropriate choice of currents and conductor shapes.

articleTitle: Influence of Sputtering Ar Pressure on Characteristics of Tb-Co Amorphous Thain Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Amorphous Tb-Co films were prepared by diode RF sputtering under various Ar gas pressures and without applying a bias voltage, which is known to induce a large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. The coercive force, saturation magnetization, and perpendicular anisotropy energy were measured as functions of the Ar pressure, and it was found that at higher pressures a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was induced. Measurements of the film density and oxygen-content indicated that a large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy is induced for high oxygen contents and low atomic packing densities.

articleTitle: Magneto-optical Branching Waveguides and Their Application to Nonreciprocal Optical Devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The branching waveguide principle underlyring guided-wave devices is described, and an application to nonreciprocal devices is discussed. Branching waveguides are classified into two types: a symmetric type operating as a power divider, and an asymmetric mode-splitter type. A 3-dB coupler and hybrid coupler are provided with these branching waveguides. The authors indicate a possible construction of guided-wave type nonreciprocal devices such as isolators and circulators, employing 3-dB couplers, hybrid couplers, nonreciprocal phase shifters and a reciprocal phase shifter, the principle of which is the same as that of microwave hybrid type nonreciprocal circuits. The authors also describe the fabrication of a Mach-Zender interferometer on epitaxial YIG film, which is the key element for realizing the nonreciprocal devices discussed here.

articleTitle: Magnetic Moment, Curie Temperature and Invar Effects in Amorphous Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic moment, Curie temperature and Invar effects in amorphous alloys are briefly reviewed. The average magnetic moment μ of binary amorphous alloys of Fe, Co, and Ni with an early transition metal E shows a systematic trend, that is, the value of μ becomes larger as the valence and size differences between Fe, Co, Ni and E increase. Comparison of the experimental results with Friedel's model suggests that Co-E alloys exhibit strong ferromagnetism while Fe-E alloys present weak ferromagnetism. The concentration dependence of the Curie temperature T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is similar to that of μ above 20% E in Fe-E alloys. However, in the dilute concentration range, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> decreases very rapidly, resulting in spin glass behavior due to spin frustration. Invar effects such as a large thermal expansion anomaly and a remarkable pressure effect on T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> are common in Fe-based amorphous alloys. The anomalous behavior above T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is closely related to magnetic inhomogeneity.

articleTitle: Effects of Easy Axis Rotation on Magnetic Properties in (110) [001] Si-Fe with Low Thickness
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of the in-plane orientation of the [001] axis α on the sheet thickness dependences of the loss and magnetostriction in ultra-thin silicon steel sheets is discussed. Power losses were seen to decrease with the sheet thickness in the range 0.3 to 0.06 mm; however, increases with thickness are small for α 2° compared with α = 0°. The magnetostriction, which is the source of iron core noise, was also found to decrease when the sheet thickness was decreased.

articleTitle: Thickness Dependence of Induced Magnetic Anisotropy in Evaporated Permalloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The uniaxial magnetic anisotropy (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>) of evaporated Permalloy films of different thicknesses was measured. For thinner films, measurements relied on the magnetoresistive (ΔR) effect. Although there was considerable scattering in the results, K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> tended to decrease as films were made thinner than 500 Å, and disappeared at around 100 to 300 Å. This decrease is thought to be related to the island structure of extremely thin films, in which case the anisotropy finally disappears in fine crystal grains of size arotund 100 Å.

articleTitle: Stabilizing Stripe Domain by Grooving Garnet Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The possibility of forming grooves in garnet film to stabilize many parallel stripe domains at once was investigated experimentally. Grooves of width 4 to 5 μm and spaced at pitches of from 10 to 20 μm were formed by photolithography and ion milling, and various bias fields and in-plane magnetic fields were applied. Though stripe domains could be formed within the grooves, and could be made to bulge outward on one side, it was found difficult to generate stripe domains which extended outward on both sides, surrounding the groove.

abstract: The two facing targets sputtering technique is used to fabricate Co-Cr films in order to investigate the relations between the microstructure and Cr segregation and the variation in magnetic properties by analyzing the growth mechanism. It was found that the samples formed under high P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ar</sub> had H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cu</sub> values 30-50 percent higher than films formed in the medium P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ar</sub> range (0.4-10 mTorr). This seems to be due to the fact that the individual columnar particles forming these films are magnetically isolated and independent.

articleTitle: Recording and Reproducing Characteristics of Vacuum-Deposited Double-Layer Perpendicular Recording Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper reports on research into the recording and reproducing characteristics of vacuum deposited CoCr/NiFeCo double-layer perpendicular recording media. It was found that when NiFeCo film was used as the underlayer, reproducing output of the media was improved and was isotropic in plane.

articleTitle: A Study on 3 μm Period Ion-Implanted Propagation Tracks for 0.8 μmø Bubble
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Attempts to use 0.8 μm diameter bubble material to obtain ion-implanted propagation tracks with a 3 × 3 μm cell size were described. Two track shapes ("CD" and "snake" types) were used, and the period in bubble propagation direction λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> and period between adjacent tracks λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf> were varied. For a 3 × 3 μm cell size, snake type tracks resulted in broader operating margins, but CD type tracks were found to yield better performance for smaller cell sizes. It was concluded that by varying track parameters, ion-implanted propagation tracks of cell size 3 × 3 μm and using 0.8 μm diameter bubbles may be realized.
